note: Korea admits without a visa (Immigration Act art. 7(2)) the nationals of the countries with which it has a visa waiver agreement, for the stay each agreement sets (B-1), and those of the countries the Minister of Justice designates for visa-free entry (B-2), as HiKorea's tables give them (agreements as of 4 December 2024, ordinary passports only; designations, 45 countries). Agreements suspended for ordinary passports (Bangladesh, Pakistan, Liberia) are taken as visas; Uruguay's ordinary-passport waiver states no stay; Russia's 60 days are within 90 in any 180. Since 1 September 2021 every one of them needs a K-ETA before boarding (the eligible are the B-1 and B-2 countries), except the 22 the Ministry of Justice has exempted until 31 December 2026 (Australia, Austria, Belgium, Canada, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Poland, Singapore, Spain, Sweden, the United Kingdom, the United States, Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan); travellers 17 and under or 65 and over are also exempt, not modelled. Jeju's own visa-free entry and the transit schemes aren't modelled. Every other passport needs a visa.

sources.title: EY Tax News, Korea extends Temporary Electronic Travel Authorization exemption until 31 December 2026 (5 January 2026)
sources.said: The Ministry of Justice extended the temporary exemption period in connection with the Korea Electronic Travel Authorization (K-ETA) for residents of 22 jurisdictions until 31 December 2026. The temporary exemption applies to nationals of Australia, Austria, Belgium, Canada, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Poland, Singapore, Spain, Sweden, the United Kingdom and the United States (including Guam), and residents of Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan.
